rulebook.title: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 (dimensions and fouls unchanged from 2025/26)
rulebook.text_used: search extracts of the IFAB and FA-hosted Law files (theifab.com and thefa.com were not reachable for direct reading)

scene.text: At most eleven players per team on the field, one of them the goalkeeper.
Each goalkeeper wears colours clearly different from all other players and the match officials.
Players wear a shirt with sleeves, shorts, socks covering the shinguards, and boots; any tape on the socks matches the sock colour.
No jewellery of any kind (necklaces, rings, bracelets, earrings, leather or rubber bands), not even taped over.
The referee on the field with two assistant referees with flags along the touchlines, level with the second-last defender; a fourth official between the technical areas.
White lines at most 12 cm wide; goal 7.32 m between the posts and 2.44 m under the crossbar; penalty area 16.5 m deep, penalty mark 11 m from the goal line; corner flags at least 1.5 m high.

fouls.title: Handball
fouls.text: Touching the ball deliberately with the hand/arm, or with a hand/arm that has made the body unnaturally bigger, is an offence; the arm starts at the bottom of the armpit.
fouls.legal: the ball touches no arm or hand (the arm starts at the bottom of the armpit)
avoid: ball touching the arm or hand of the outfield player

fouls.title: Goalkeeper handling outside the penalty area
fouls.text: The goalkeeper may handle the ball only inside their own penalty area; outside it the goalkeeper has the same handling restrictions as any other player.
fouls.legal: the goalkeeper handles the ball inside their own penalty area
avoid: goalkeeper handling the ball far outside the penalty area

fouls.title: Goalkeeper colours
fouls.text: The goalkeeper's kit must be distinguishable from the other players and the match officials.
fouls.legal: the goalkeeper wears a kit colour different from both teams and the referee
avoid: goalkeeper in the same colour as the outfield players

fouls.title: Playing in a dangerous manner
fouls.text: An action that threatens injury while playing the ball (for example a high foot near an opponent's head) is an offence; a scissors or bicycle kick is allowed if it is not dangerous to an opponent.
fouls.legal: no opponent's head is near the raised boot
avoid: boot swinging at an opponent's head

fouls.title: Arms and elbows in an aerial duel
fouls.text: Striking, pushing or holding an opponent with the hand or arm, or leading with the elbow into the head or face, is an offence (violent conduct if deliberate).
fouls.legal: the raised arms do not strike or hold an opponent

fouls.title: Jewellery
fouls.text: All jewellery is forbidden and must be removed; covering it with tape is not permitted.
